title: What senior care costs in New Jersey
dek: Home care, adult day, assisted living and nursing homes, with the latest CareScout figures for New Jersey, how they compare nationally and how families pay.
keyFacts: Source: CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2025 (prices collected July to Nov. 2025)
NJ home care: $38 an hour median
NJ adult day health care: $100 a day
NJ assisted living: $8,710 a month; nursing home semi-private: $12,775 a month
Costs vary by region and provider; always get written quotes
body:
Long-term care is one of the biggest costs many families ever face, and New Jersey is one of the more expensive states for it. Knowing the numbers early helps you plan, compare options and avoid decisions made in a rush after a hospital stay.

This guide uses the most recent figures from CareScout's Cost of Care Survey 2025. The survey has run since 2004 and was long published under the Genworth name. CareScout collected prices from care providers between July and November 2025 and published the results in March 2026.

The numbers at a glance

Type of care (NJ median, 2025)RateMonthlyYearly
Home care, non-medical caregiver$38 an hour$7,245 at 44 hrs/week$86,944
Adult day health care$100 a day$2,167 at 5 days/week$26,000
Assisted living, private one-bedroom$286 a day$8,710$104,520
Nursing home, semi-private room$420 a day$12,775$153,300
Nursing home, private room$475 a day$14,448$173,375

Source: CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2025, median cost data tables. Monthly home care is based on 44 hours a week. Adult day is based on 5 days a week.

How does New Jersey compare?

New Jersey is above the national median in every category CareScout reports:

  • Home care: $38 an hour in New Jersey, $35 nationally.
  • Adult day health care: $100 a day in New Jersey, $95 nationally.
  • Assisted living: $8,710 a month in New Jersey, $6,200 nationally.
  • Nursing home, semi-private: $12,775 a month in New Jersey, $9,581 nationally.
  • Nursing home, private: $14,448 a month in New Jersey, $10,798 nationally.

CareScout ranked New Jersey 13th highest in the country for a semi-private nursing home room and 12th for a private room.

Why your costs may be different

These are medians, which means half of providers charge more and half charge less. CareScout collects data by metro area and notes that actual costs depend on care needs, provider availability and local market conditions. Prices in North Jersey near New York City can differ from those in the Pine Barrens or at the shore.

Other things that move the price:

  • Level of care. Many assisted living residences charge more as needs increase.
  • Memory care. CareScout does not report it separately. Residences set their own memory care rates. Ask for them in writing.
  • Hours and schedule. Home care agencies may charge more for short visits, nights, weekends or holidays.
  • Room type. A private nursing home room costs about $1,700 a month more than a semi-private room at the median.
Use the medians to plan. Use written quotes to decide.

Questions to ask when you get a quote

A low advertised rate can grow once extras are added. Ask each provider:

  • What exactly is included in the base price, and what costs extra?
  • Is there a minimum number of hours per visit or per week?
  • How much notice do you give before a price increase, and how often have prices gone up?
  • Is there an entrance or community fee, and is any of it refundable?
  • Do you accept Medicaid, long-term care insurance or veterans benefits?
  • Can I have the full fee schedule and contract in writing?

Write the answers down for each place. Comparing side by side makes the real differences easier to see.

A few examples

These hypothetical examples use the 2025 medians:

  • Light help at home. An aide 4 hours a day, 3 days a week: 12 hours at $38 is $456 a week, or about $1,980 a month.
  • Adult day plus some aide hours. Adult day 3 days a week at $100 a day is $300 a week. Add 10 hours of aide help at $38 and the total is $680 a week, or about $2,950 a month.
  • Full days at home. 44 hours a week of home care is $7,245 a month, plus the cost of running the house.
  • Assisted living. $8,710 a month, which includes housing and meals.
  • Nursing home. $12,775 a month for a semi-private room.

Adult day health care can be a good value for keeping someone home. It gives a family caregiver the day to work or rest. See our respite care guide.

Who pays for long-term care?

Medicare

Medicare does not pay for long-term custodial care, at home, in assisted living or in a nursing home. It does cover short skilled nursing stays after a qualifying hospital stay, up to 100 days per benefit period. In 2026, days 21 to 100 cost $217 a day. See our hospital discharge guide.

NJ Medicaid (MLTSS)

New Jersey's Managed Long Term Services and Supports program can pay for care at home, assisted living and nursing homes for people who meet financial rules and need a nursing home level of care. Learn the rules early in our MLTSS guide.

Other sources

  • Long-term care insurance, if your parent bought a policy.
  • Veterans benefits. Ask your county veterans service office whether any apply.
  • Savings, retirement accounts and home equity.
  • Family contributions. Put any family arrangement in writing.
Ways to lower costs

Check every benefit your parent may qualify for. New Jersey's PAAD and Senior Gold lower drug costs, and property tax relief programs can ease the cost of staying home. See prescription and bill help and property tax relief. For a free screening, call the Aging and Disability Resource Connection at 1-877-222-3737.

How to use these numbers

  1. List what help is needed now and what may be needed in a year.
  2. Estimate the monthly cost of each option using the table above.
  3. Add up income and savings, and figure out how many months they cover.
  4. Get written quotes from two or three local providers. See our guides to choosing a home care agency and assisted living vs. home care.
  5. Talk with an elder law attorney before savings run low. See estate planning in NJ.

A geriatric care manager can also assess needs and give you a realistic local picture of costs and options.

faq.q: How much does home care cost per hour in New Jersey?
faq.a: CareScout's 2025 Cost of Care Survey put the New Jersey median for a non-medical home care worker at $38 an hour, compared with $35 nationally. Rates vary by region and agency.

faq.q: What is the average cost of assisted living in NJ?
faq.a: CareScout's 2025 median for a private one-bedroom in New Jersey assisted living was $8,710 a month, or $104,520 a year. The national median was $6,200 a month.

faq.q: How much is a nursing home per month in New Jersey?
faq.a: CareScout's 2025 medians were $12,775 a month for a semi-private room and $14,448 for a private room in New Jersey.

faq.q: How much does adult day care cost in New Jersey?
faq.a: CareScout's 2025 median for adult day health care in New Jersey was $100 a day, or about $2,167 a month at five days a week.

faq.q: Does Medicare pay for long-term care in NJ?
faq.a: No. Medicare does not pay for long-term custodial care. NJ Medicaid's MLTSS program can pay for home care, assisted living and nursing homes for people who qualify.

faq.q: How much does memory care cost in NJ?
faq.a: CareScout does not publish a separate memory care figure. Each residence sets its own rate, often on top of assisted living pricing, so ask for written quotes.
